idea-plugin.name: Sightline
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Code inside Android Studio, with visible project activity and controlled tool execution.

Sightline provides a native Android Studio interface for a locally installed Claude Code CLI.

Use it to:

  • Chat with Claude without leaving Android Studio.
  • Attach files and IDE context, and remove any of it before you send.
  • Review tool requests and proposed changes as diffs before they apply.
  • See files, commands, tests and relationships in the Activity Map.
  • Inspect structured build, test and diagnostic results.

Android-aware. Sightline knows your build variant, connected device, module and running process, so you don't have to explain them. It reads Gradle failures into typed diagnoses, resolves crashes back to the line that threw, picks the tests worth running for what you changed, and audits your merged manifest. Logcat is redacted before it can reach a prompt.

Requires the Claude Code CLI (the claude command), installed and authenticated separately. Sightline does not provide Claude access, does not handle your credentials, and has no login screen or backend of its own.

No telemetry. No analytics, no usage statistics, nothing sent anywhere except to the local claude process you started. Your conversation is never written to disk.

Sightline is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic, JetBrains or Google. "Claude" and "Claude Code" are trademarks of Anthropic; "Android Studio" is a trademark of Google. Both are used only to describe compatibility.

idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.7.0

  • MCP servers you add show up in the conversation you already have open. Run claude mcp add playwright … while you are mid-conversation and its tools become available right where you are — no restart, no lost context. Sightline reports what changed: which servers were added, how many tools each brought, and the CLI's own reason if one could not start.
  • It stays out of your way. Nothing waits on the sync, and a change noticed mid-turn is applied once that turn ends. Servers from the project's checked-in .mcp.json are reported but not started for you — that file can arrive from a git pull — and they load with your next conversation.
  • Server configurations can carry credentials, so they go to the CLI and nowhere else: never a log, never the transcript. Switch the whole feature off in Settings if you would rather it only reported.

0.6.0

  • Switch models from the composer. The / actions menu has a Model submenu — the CLI's aliases, any full model id you pin, and a line reporting what the CLI says it is actually running. Switching mid-conversation takes effect in place, keeping the session and the conversation.
  • Wide tables render again. A Markdown table whose cells were wider than the chat column showed as an empty bordered box; it now scrolls horizontally instead.
  • Themes behave. The Activity Map no longer renders its toolbar as dark strips around a correctly light graph, and the panel follows a theme you switch while it is open.

0.5.0 — first stable release, and the point at which the supported platform narrowed to Android Studio Quail 2 (2026.1.2) or later. IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1+ is the same platform build and can still install Sightline, with the Android features degrading as they always have.

Earlier releases, and the reasoning behind each change, are in CHANGELOG.md in the repository.
